newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Refinancing drives Australia housing rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Refinancing drives Australia housing rise.

text.p: The Australian housing industry said on Monday the rise in September housing finance showed the real estate market was strengthening.
Finance commitments for owner-occupied housing rose 5.8 percent seasonally-adjusted to 42,272 dwellings in September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Monday.
The Real Estate Institute of Australia said the figures showed a strengthening in the real estate market, marked by more sales and refinancing.

Institute President Don Brindley said in a statement new building remained weak with finance commitments of new dwellings rising 2.4 percent seasonally-adjusted to 5,507 from 4,937 the previous month.
Housing Industry Association Managing Director Ron Silberberg said in a statement the rise in housing finance commitments was in line with market expectations.

Colonial State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen said refinancing continued to pay a major role in the housing finance market, with September data showing that 29.2 percent of the lending committed in September was refinancing.
"If refinancing is taken out of the figures, the recent pick up in lending activity does not look as healthy," Kunnen said.

Westpac Banking Corp economists said in a report that the overall picture of housing finance continued to be distorted by the increasing competition between bank and non-bank lenders for increased market share in the home lending market.
"This latest data further confirms that housing sector activity has definitely troughed but at this stage is still not signalling any substantive rebound," Westpac said.
